steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: Narrative writing tells a story with a beginning, middle, and end. It features characters, a plot with events, a setting, and often explores themes through conflict and resolution. | The Five-Part Structure: Exposition: Introduce characters, setting, situation Rising Action: Build tension through complications Climax: The turning point or peak of tension Falling Action: Consequences of the climax Resolution: Loose ends tied up, new equilibrium | Show Character Through Action: Instead of telling us someone is brave, show them facing fear. Instead of telling us someone is kind, show them helping another character. | Dialogue Rules: Each character should have a distinct voice Keep it realistic - people interrupt, trail off, use incomplete sentences Avoid info-dumps - don't use dia

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What are the five parts of a classic story arc? | What does "in medias res" mean and why is it effective? | Name two ways to reveal character without directly stating traits.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on The Five-Part Structure, Show Character Through Action, Dialogue Rules, and one past-paper question.
